questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I could speak and understand the language. I really wanted to explore other Nordic countries and feel closer to Scandinavia. And then the nature in Norway of course.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. There was a lot of introduction and events and so on. And everyone from UiB were really nice to answer all our question via email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I needed help with courses and I changed courses at one point, so that was my primary concern. And then I needed help finding psychologist and Sammen at UiB also helped with that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The only thing was that the student organized welcome was centered a lot on drinking and a bit messy. Messy in like organization and planning... so I didn't have the best experience there and didn't go to all the events. But I heard a lot of other people on other faculties had a good experience

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I only send one email and got the room

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's lovely getting to know a local. It felt as I was a part of the Bergen student community and not only and exchange community. My roommate showed me all sorts of things and it is so nice knowing someone in Bergen now.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Just a lot of paper works, but besides that it was easy enough

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to apply for acceptance of your courses and that decides whether you can get your courses or not. My institute are very sweet and open so they say yes to almost everything, so that really nice when you go on exchange and want to try something else. And then regarding choosing university I just looked in Mobility One. And then I have a coordinator here in Denmark who answered all my questions. I also went to a zoom meeting twice about exchange.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a zoom meeting, a physical meeting and then a coordinator. And also a Facebook group for all KU students going to the Nordic countries

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. 10 out of 10. I also changed courses doing my stay.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any problems so I don't know if I have any advice. Maybe talk to your coordinator and ask questions if you are afraid that you can't get your courses. Check and see how open your university is with you taking different courses

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It felt easier than was I was used to at Copenhagen. But I think that might be because I had more time and didn't have a job either. I had peace to focus on my studies and that gave me a chance to be really well prepared.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same, but in a smaller class which I enjoyed a lot. That gives more room for conversation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Electronic Literature
Current Anthropological Research: New Technologies and the Future of the Human
The Frontier of Anthropological Research: Times of War. Cultural and Symbolic Landscapes in Contemporary Eastern Europe

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the above. I study anthropology and tried courses on Digital Culture which was really nice. If your university allows it try something else. Maybe more practical or a different subject that you are used to. It's fun for you and it's really nice for your brain to try and think differently. I came back to Copenhagen with more energy to study again and a new way of seeing different dilemmas

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to go to the doctor a lot, so that. And then also trips and climbing. I didn't count on going on that many trips but then I ended up renting a car and so on. But personal experience and costs but still unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transportation! So cheap compared to DK

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined a student bar - diskuterbar. Would a 100% recommend. Made my whole semester. Volunteer some place.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts. BSI is so great at offering different stuff. There is literally anything. And if you don't find anything Bergen is a city of culture, so I'm pretty sure you can find something.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Volunteer, join a sport or a student club. Go to local events

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take the train an hour away and hike. Take a car to Sotra (lovely!!!). Go to Kanadaskogen and look for mushrooms. Swim in the fjord. Go to søbadet. Go to the club Rommet or Landmark or Kulturhuset. Go fishing. Take the boat. Go for a walk in Sandviken

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I took about a month but it felt easy in retrospect. But I also joined a student club and the helped tremendously.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was easy because I speak danish, but... Maybe try and find activities where there is a mix of international and norwegian students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None. Maybe the age gap a little bit. I was 25 and a lot of bachelor students in Norway are way younger. But I didn't bother. And I met plenty of peers

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Nature:) People, so kind:)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join something. Be a volunteer or join a sport anything. It helps a lot when you are new.
Say yes a lot.
If you want a more local experience then try to find housing on your own with other norwegian students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't live at Fantoft, but I heard that a lot of international students enjoyed it and it creates friends and some social ties pretty quick. So if you fear loneliness I would recommend going there. But I would still recommend trying to find housing with Norwegian students and get a more local experience.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people, the break from my everyday, the nature

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Settling in. The first month I cried a lot haha. I felt introduction week (fadderuken) was horrible, but then I found my people and then everything turned around. And classes began and I love learning new things

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
